Laredo ISD Board of Trustees candidates took the stage Oct. 14 at MileOne for a debate on the district's priorities and challenges — but only two of the four candidates showed up, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The forum, organized by the nonpartisan groups MOVE Texas, STX Frontera, CMPSCHL Creative, and the Carnalismo Brown Berets and moderated by retired TAMIU professor Dr. John Kilburn, covered two contested races: District 3, where incumbent Veronica V. Orduño faces Priscilla Treviño, and District 6, where incumbent Dr. Gilberto "Gil" Martinez faces Hector "Tito" Garcia. Only the two incumbents attended.

Both Orduño and Martinez are four-year trustees and career educators — Orduño a former teacher, Martinez with more than 25 years in the classroom and fine-arts degrees in theater.

On the issues, both candidates backed transparency and accountability measures including online meeting streams and public comment. They pointed to a deficit trimmed from $20 million to $8 million, with a commitment to cut administrative positions before touching teachers, using attrition and retirements. On declining enrollment and campus consolidation, they said no campuses have been closed, noting part of Cigarroa Middle School was repurposed as the Rise Academy.

Both supported two teacher planning periods and a 45-minute lunch, with Martinez floating a teacher advisory board. They discussed closing the achievement gap with an early-grades focus, serving special education, gifted and talented, and advanced students, and balancing college prep with career and technical education — including industry certifications and health care partnerships in areas like Alzheimer's, dementia, and geriatric care. They also pledged to protect arts programs — band, theater, music, visual arts — and athletics, to welcome all students regardless of immigration status, and to keep improving employee compensation.

Early voting is already underway in Webb County ahead of the Nov. 3 election.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times (Oct. 19, 2026).

title: Two LISD incumbents face challengers as trustee candidates debate priorities — two no-shows
